guide.title: About 3GP and MP4
guide.markdown:
### What is a 3GP file?

3GP is a container format defined by the 3rd Generation Partnership Project for video on mobile phones. It specializes the ISO base media file format, the same family MP4 belongs to, and it is a simplified version of the MP4 container that keeps files small. It serves mobile messaging, downloads and packet-switched streaming, and a single presentation may mix video, speech, other audio and timed text.

The standard registers several video codecs, including H.263, MPEG-4 Visual, AVC and HEVC. For sound it registers AMR variants and AAC. A file extension does not identify which of the permitted codecs a 3GP recording contains, which is why two .3gp files can behave very differently. You meet 3GP files from older mobile phones and in MMS video. A conforming file includes a file-type box whose brands identify its profile.

### Programs that open 3GP files

- **Linux, Mac and Windows:** FFmpeg reads 3GP containers, and VLC media player accepts 3GP input.
- **Windows:** Windows Media Player opens 3GP.
- **Mac:** QuickTime Player opens 3GP.

The codecs inside the file decide what a player can do with it.

### 3GP and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .3gp with video/3gpp for visual content and audio/3gpp for purely audio content; .mp4 with video/mp4 and audio/mp4.
- **Container family**: both descend from the ISO base media file format, itself an outgrowth of Apple's QuickTime format. MP4 is ISO/IEC 14496-14, first published in 2003.
- **Video codecs**: 3GP registers the four listed above. MP4 commonly holds H.264 (AVC), and can also carry H.265, AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus.
- **Audio**: 3GP registers AMR variants and AAC. MP4 commonly carries AAC.
- **Extras**: MP4 can hold subtitles and chapters. Its boxes nest inside one another, a structure QuickTime knows as atoms.
- **Used for**: 3GP serves video on older mobile phones and MMS video. MP4 is used for online video and streaming, for phone and camera recordings, and for passing video around.
- **Files**: video MP4 files use .mp4 or .m4v, and audio-only MPEG-4 files often use .m4a.
- **Reach**: every major browser plays MP4, and it plays on nearly every device. Android 5.0 added HEVC playback inside MP4 files.

Your browser runs FFmpeg as WebAssembly to decode the 3GP and encode the result. Video becomes H.264 with libx264 at CRF 32, using the ultrafast preset, and audio becomes AAC at 96 kbps. This page always re-encodes and never copies the streams, and no stream mapping is passed, which leaves FFmpeg's defaults to choose the streams. Frame size carries over unless the long side exceeds 1920 pixels, and frame rate carries over unless it exceeds 30 fps. Interlaced frames, if any, are deinterlaced first. The MP4 is written with the index at the front (faststart).

Several 3GP files can be chosen at once. They are processed in sequence, and every result downloads separately, with no ZIP, under your file's name and the .mp4 ending. Your original 3GP is not changed.

### Other ways to convert 3GP to MP4

- **FFmpeg (command line):** enter `ffmpeg -i phone.3gp -c:v libx264 -c:a aac phone.mp4`. FFmpeg's mov demuxer lists the 3gp extension, and both streams are re-encoded.
- **VLC (Windows, Mac, Linux):** choose Media > Convert/Save, click Add and pick the 3GP, type the destination file name, choose a conversion profile from the Profile drop-down and click Start. VLC lists 3GP among its input formats.

### Problems with 3GP files

- **The file won't open on a modern device**: the .3gp ending doesn't show which codecs are inside, so the device may lack one of them. Converting writes H.264 video and AAC sound.
- **A player shows less than another tool**: a conforming parser is allowed to skip boxes or codecs the specification does not cover, so two programs may disagree about one file.
- **The video is tiny**: 3GP keeps files small, and a recording can have a small frame. Conversion cannot add detail, because a small frame is never scaled up.
- **There is sound but no picture**: an audio-only 3GP has no video track to recover, and the format explicitly permits pure sound.
- **The MP4 is larger than the 3GP**: the page encodes the MP4 to a fixed quality (CRF 32) instead of a target size, so the size can go either way.

faqs.question: How do I convert AAC to MP3?

faqs.question: How do I change AAC to MP3 at a different bitrate?

faqs.question: Does converting AAC to MP3 lose quality?

faqs.question: Will the MP3 be bigger than my AAC file?

faqs.question: What is the difference between .aac and .m4a?

faqs.question: Why would I turn AAC into MP3?
faqs.answer: MP3 plays on nearly every device, and every major browser plays it. Some older players and car stereos read MP3 but not AAC.

faqs.question: Why won't my player open this AAC file?

faqs.question: Will the MP3 have the same tags and sample rate?

faqs.question: Why does the converter report that FFmpeg failed?
faqs.answer: FFmpeg could not decode audio from the file, for example because it is another format with an .aac name. Open it in VLC to check.

faqs.question: Is there a limit on file size or length?
faqs.answer: Nothing in the page caps size or length. Your own device does the work, so long recordings take longer on slower hardware.

guide.title: About AAC files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AAC file?

AAC (Advanced Audio Coding) belongs to the MPEG family of perceptual audio codecs. MPEG-2 defines it in Part 7 and MPEG-4 in Part 3, under the ISO/IEC numbers 13818-7 and 14496-3. The profiles you will meet are LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2. It carries streaming audio and music downloads, the sound in MP4 videos and audio on mobile devices. It was designed as MP3's successor and generally sounds better at the same bitrate.

AAC names the coding alone, which is why it travels in different wrappers. Inside MP4 or QuickTime it becomes an .m4a-style file, while a standalone .aac file commonly uses ADTS framing. The registered media type audio/aac spans ADTS and LATM/LOAS transport. Two files with the .aac name can therefore behave differently in different players.

### Programs that open AAC files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- FFmpeg: includes AAC decoding and an internal AAC encoder. It is a command-line tool, and it is also the engine this page runs.
- VLC media player: accepts raw AAC input and decodes MPEG-4 AAC audio. It is free and plays the file without converting it first.

**Windows and Mac**

- Adobe Audition: imports AAC, including HE-AAC. It is a paid editor, useful when you want to trim or clean the recording before exporting.

**Web**

- Firefox and Chrome play AAC in the browser, though availability can depend on system codecs.

### AAC and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .aac with audio/aac; .mp3 with audio/mpeg.
- **Origin**: MP3 (MPEG-1 Audio Layer III) became ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993, and ISO/IEC 13818-3 extended it in 1995. Fraunhofer IIS and fellow MPEG audio group members started development in the late 1980s.
- **Compression**: both formats are lossy and lean on a model of hearing to drop sound you are unlikely to miss. An MP3 at 128 kbit/s is about an eleventh of the size of the CD audio behind it.
- **Bitrates**: the sample rate is 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz and the bitrate runs from 32 up to 320 kbps.
- **Metadata**: MP3 keeps titles and other tags in ID3 blocks inside the file.
- **Patents**: licensing for MP3 patents ended on 23 April 2017.
- **Container**: AAC is only the coding, so it can sit in an MP4 or QuickTime wrapper or stand alone with ADTS framing. MP3 is its own stream format, with ID3 blocks for tags.
- **Support**: every major browser plays MP3. For AAC, Firefox availability can depend on system codecs, so an AAC file that plays on one computer may stay silent on another.
- **Efficiency**: AAC generally sounds better than MP3 at the same bitrate.

In this converter, FFmpeg runs in your browser, decodes the AAC, then LAME encodes an MP3, asking for 192 kbit/s. Below 32 kHz, MP3 can't reach 192 kbit/s, so LAME writes a lower rate. The MP3 is a second lossy generation of the sound. The page does not pick audio tracks, trim or change volume. Each AAC is converted by itself in turn, and the MP3 download takes the AAC's name; the original stays as it was. The page sets no size limit, so a long recording only takes longer.

### Other ways to convert AAC to MP3

- **FFmpeg in a terminal:** enter `ffmpeg -i lecture.aac -codec:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k lecture.mp3`. FFmpeg does the AAC decoding. The -codec:a option picks the audio encoder, and -b:a sets its bitrate.

### Problems with AAC files

- **One .aac opens and another doesn't**: the audio/aac media type covers both ADTS and LATM/LOAS transport, so two files with the same name can need different support from the player.
- **A player won't open it**: an MPEG-2 AAC decoder can fail on MPEG-4 variants. Try VLC, or convert the file to MP3.
- **Renaming to .m4a doesn't help**: changing .aac to .m4a does not replace ADTS framing with an MP4 wrapper. The file still holds the same data.
- **The decoded copy is huge**: AAC stores compressed audio, so decoding it to an uncompressed form, as an editor does while you work, takes far more space.
- **Zipping saves almost nothing**: ZIP compression usually offers little extra reduction for AAC streams, because the audio is already compressed.

faqs.question: Will the JPG keep my editable paths and layers?

faqs.question: How large will the JPG be?

faqs.question: How do I get a specific resolution?

faqs.question: Why are my linked images missing?

faqs.question: Can I convert an AI file from a very old Illustrator?
faqs.answer: Not directly. The oldest AI files were based on PostScript and have no PDF inside, so this page refuses them with the "no PDF inside" message. Opening one in a current Illustrator and saving it as a PDF-compatible AI gives you a file this page accepts.

guide.title: About AI and JPG
guide.markdown:
### What is an AI file?

Adobe Illustrator saves its artwork natively as AI. A single document may combine vector objects and pixel images, and Illustrator keeps effects, brushes, layers and transparency editable inside it. Typical AI documents are logos, illustrations and print layouts.

Adobe changed the AI format with Illustrator 9 in 2000, and earlier files used PostScript. Saving with the PDF-compatible option puts a PDF rendition next to the Illustrator data, and that PDF part is all other apps can open. A program that reads the embedded PDF does not necessarily expose native Illustrator objects for editing. That rendition is also what this converter reads.

### Programs that open AI files

- **Windows and Mac:** Native artwork opens in Adobe Illustrator with its Illustrator objects still editable.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads the AI format its list calls Adobe Illustrator CS2, so it renders the artwork but does not edit it as Illustrator does.
- **Linux:** Inkscape's manual says it imports AI artwork from Illustrator 9.0 onward, with some document features possibly unavailable.

Affinity Designer and CorelDRAW are also listed among the programs that open AI files.

### AI and JPG compared

- **Content**: AI holds vector paths, text, layers and artboards. JPG holds a grid of pixels.
- **Editing**: a JPEG has no editable layer stack, so keep the AI if the artwork will change later.
- **Transparency**: with no alpha channel in JPEG, transparent pixels can't make it through the export. This page draws each page on white.
- **Compression**: JPEG is a lossy format with 8 bits for every color channel. A progressive JPEG displays a rough picture right away, and later data sharpens it.
- **Standards**: image/jpeg is the registered media type, and the specification is ITU-T T.81 from 1992, also published as ISO/IEC 10918-1 in 1994.
- **How JPEG compresses**: in the baseline form, 8x8 pixel blocks of the image each get a discrete cosine transform, followed by Huffman coding.
- **Support**: most digital cameras and scanners have JPEG built in, all major browsers display it, and 27 October 2006 is when the US patents ran out.
- **Print and screen**: AI is aimed at logos, illustrations and print layouts, while JPG is built for photographs and displays in every major browser.
- **Size**: vector artwork can be drawn at any size, while a JPG is fixed at the pixel size it was rendered at.

On this page, PDF.js reads the PDF inside the AI file and renders every page. PDF.js draws each page at a scale of up to 2, reduced for a big page so its area stays within 16,777,216 pixels. Each page becomes its own JPG at quality 0.9 on a white background, and the pages arrive as separate images, not one combined file. The AI file itself is not changed.

Because the page reads only the embedded PDF, the JPG shows the page as that PDF draws it. Keep the AI for any later edit, because the JPG holds only pixels.

### Other ways to convert AI to JPG

- **ImageMagick (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `magick -density 150 input.ai output.jpg`. ImageMagick's format list shows AI as a format it reads, and the -density option sets the canvas resolution while rendering vector formats such as PostScript and PDF.
- **Ghostscript (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `gs -dBATCH -dNOPAUSE -sDEVICE=jpeg -r150 -sOutputFile=page-%d.jpg input.ai`. The -r option takes the resolution, and %d in the output name is replaced with the page number, so each page gets its own file. It reads the PDF part of a PDF-compatible AI, not Illustrator's editable objects.

Both commands render at the resolution you set, unlike this page, which chooses its own scale.

### Problems with AI files

- **Other software can't open it**: third-party software may fail on an AI file that was saved with no PDF-compatible representation. Save it again from Illustrator with that option on.
- **Opening in an older Illustrator**: an older Illustrator version may run into compatibility problems with the artwork, so Adobe recommends the same or a newer version.
- **A linked image is missing**: the artwork may point at an external image instead of holding it, so a moved or absent file leaves a gap.
- **A very old file has no PDF**: files from before Illustrator 9 were based on PostScript, so there is no PDF rendition for other software to read.

faqs.answer: Select the files together and they are rendered one after another, each page of each file downloading as its own PNG.

faqs.question: Is my artwork uploaded when I convert it?
faqs.answer: No. The PDF inside your AI file is rendered in your browser with PDF.js, so the file stays on your device.

guide.title: Understanding AI for PNG output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AI file?

AI is Adobe Illustrator's native artwork format. An AI document can hold vector objects next to pixel images, and Illustrator keeps editable effects, brushes, layers and transparency inside the file. AI source files are what designers work from for logos, illustrations and print layouts.

Illustrator 9 changed the AI format in 2000; earlier files used PostScript. The PDF-compatible saving option includes a PDF rendition alongside the Illustrator data, and that rendition is what this page draws. Modern files embed that PDF-compatible stream, which is why other programs can often read an AI file without owning Illustrator.

You will usually receive an AI file from a designer or a brand kit. To put the artwork in a slide, a web page or a document, you need a picture instead. Keep the AI itself if the artwork may need editing.

### Programs that open AI files

- **Mac and Windows:** Adobe Illustrator opens native artwork and keeps its Illustrator objects editable.
- **Linux, Mac and Windows:** ImageMagick can read the AI format that its format list calls Illustrator CS2, but it renders the artwork rather than editing it as Illustrator does.
- **Linux:** Inkscape's import manual lists Illustrator files from version 9.0 onward, though not every document feature is available.

### AI and PNG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .ai, a proprietary Adobe format; .png with image/png.
- **What is stored**: an AI keeps vector artwork, layers and artboards. A PNG keeps pixels as indexed, grayscale or truecolor samples of 1 to 16 bits each.
- **Compression**: PNG compression is always lossless, using the DEFLATE method, so a rendered logo stays crisp at the size it was drawn.
- **Transparency**: PNG supports an optional alpha channel, but this page paints a white background.
- **History**: PNG was designed as a patent-free alternative to GIF, and RFC 2083 and ISO/IEC 15948:2004 later defined it.
- **Structure**: the first thing in a PNG is a fixed signature, and after it come chunks: the header sits in IHDR, the image data in IDAT, and IEND ends the file.
- **Standards**: October 1996 saw PNG published as the first format to become a W3C Recommendation.
- **Support**: PNG is displayed by every major browser, and no known patents on it require royalties.
- **Editing**: the AI can be reopened and changed. The PNG is a final picture, and changing it means editing pixels.

The page renders each page of the embedded PDF with PDF.js. A page is drawn at up to twice its size, and scaled down if it would pass 16,777,216 pixels, about 16.8 megapixels. The cap is on area, not on each side. Pages are drawn onto opaque white and are not merged into one picture. Each page downloads as its own PNG, named after the file with _page1, _page2 and so on, and your AI is never changed. Because only the embedded PDF is drawn, the result shows the artwork as it was saved into that rendition, not as a live document.

### Other ways to convert AI to PNG

- **Inkscape (Windows, Mac, Linux):** bring the AI file into Inkscape and use File > Export PNG Image, or press Shift+Ctrl+E. Choose what to export from Page, Drawing, Selection or Custom, under Image Size set the pixel dimensions or the resolution, pick a file name and press Export.
- **ImageMagick (command line):** run `magick artwork.ai artwork.png`. ImageMagick's format list marks AI as both readable and writable, under the name Adobe Illustrator CS2. The result is a rendering, not an editable file.

### Problems with AI files

- **"This AI file has no PDF inside"**: the file was saved without a PDF-compatible representation. In Illustrator, save it again with Create PDF Compatible File turned on. Older PostScript-based files don't have it.
- **Third-party software can't read the AI**: a file saved without its PDF-compatible representation may fail in other programs as well.
- **Linked pictures are missing**: Illustrator leaves linked images outside the file unless Include Linked Files is chosen when saving.
- **Illustrator reports a compatibility problem**: opening artwork in an older Illustrator version can cause them, so Adobe advises matching or newer versions.
- **You need to edit the design**: a program that reads the embedded PDF doesn't necessarily expose the native objects. Keep the AI.
- **Several pages came out**: that is expected when the embedded PDF has more than one page. Each is its own PNG.

faqs.question: Why is the MP3 so much smaller than the AIF?

faqs.question: Is there a limit on how long an AIF can be?

faqs.question: Does the AIF leave my computer?
faqs.answer: No. The conversion engine, FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly, loads into this page, so there is nothing to install and no upload. You download a new MP3 and the AIF stays as it was.

guide.title: About AIF and MP3
guide.markdown:
### What is an AIF file?

An AIF file is an Audio Interchange File Format recording. The .aif extension is the short form of .aiff, and both name the same format. AIFF was Apple's creation, based on Electronic Arts' IFF family, and version 1.3 of its specification carries the date January 4, 1989. Uncompressed linear PCM samples are the usual contents, while AIFF-C widens the family to compressed audio. An AIFF can also include named chunks for the author, copyright and annotations.

Masters and working recordings in professional audio are a typical use, and macOS audio production is where AIFF is best known. Because the samples are usually uncompressed and lossless, the files are large, and a recording is often turned into an MP3 before it is shared. Common media-type labels are audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff.

### Programs that open AIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity imports most AIFF files, every PCM variant included, without its optional FFmpeg library. It is the choice for trimming or cleaning a recording before you export it.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg lists AIFF encoding and decoding support in its format table, and it runs from the command line.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** AIFF is among the files VLC media player opens.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Audition opens uncompressed AIFF and most of the common compressed variants, which suits professional editing.
- **Mac:** Apple Music plays AIFF, and Logic Pro, Apple's music production app, opens it for editing.

### AIF and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .aif and .aiff are common audio/aiff, with audio/x-aiff also seen. MP3's registered media type is audio/mpeg.
- **Compression**: AIFF is normally uncompressed PCM. MP3 is a lossy format, and it plays in every major browser; it shrinks audio by dropping sounds that a model of human hearing says listeners won't notice.
- **Standards**: MP3 is MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, standardized as ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993 and extended by ISO/IEC 13818-3 in 1995. The late 1980s saw Fraunhofer IIS start the work on MP3, joined by other members of the MPEG audio group.
- **Size**: compared with the same audio on a CD, an MP3 at 128 kbit/s takes roughly one eleventh of the space.
- **Bitrate**: an MP3 can be written at 32 to 320 kbps, at a 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz sampling rate. This page asks for 192 kbps, so a source below 32 kHz gets a lower rate.
- **Metadata**: AIFF has its own chunks for author, copyright and annotations. ID3 structures, separate from the audio, hold an MP3's song titles and other tags.
- **Playback**: every major browser plays MP3, so the converted file works almost anywhere.
- **Licensing**: the MP3 patent licensing program ended on 23 April 2017.

This page re-encodes the audio with FFmpeg's LAME encoder and discards any picture track. The result is a standard MP3 that is not identical to the AIF. Global tags from the AIF are carried over by FFmpeg wherever the MP3 has a matching field.

### Other ways to convert AIF to MP3

- **FFmpeg (command line):** encode with `ffmpeg -i input.aif -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k output.mp3`. FFmpeg's documentation lists AIFF among the formats it reads, describes the LAME encoder, and sets the bitrate with the b option. Replace input.aif with the name of your own file, and the result is written next to it as output.mp3 in the folder where you ran the command.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** use File > Import > Audio to load the AIF, then File > Export Audio with MP3 chosen as the format. The bit rate modes are Preset, Variable, Average and Constant, and the Standard preset is the default.

Each route makes a lossy MP3, so keep the AIF as your master.

### Problems with AIF files

- **One AIF plays, another doesn't**: AIFF-C compression requires a decoder for the actual encoding, and the family name alone does not establish support.
- **Author field missing**: Adobe Audition can file an AIFF's author under Dublin Core: Creator, not under a field called Author.
- **The AIF is too big to email**: a long recording in uncompressed PCM gets very large, and a compressed copy of it takes less storage.
- **The extension misleads**: .aif and .aiff are the same format, but a file ending in either may hold AIFF-C, so the ending does not tell you how the audio is encoded.

guide.title: Understanding AIFF for MP3 output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AIFF file?

AIFF stands for Audio Interchange File Format. Apple developed it, and it is an audio wrapper derived from Electronic Arts' IFF family. Apple's AIFF 1.3 specification is dated January 4, 1989.

An AIFF often carries uncompressed linear PCM samples, which is why professional audio users have long used it for masters and intermediate recordings. The AIFF-C extension covers compressed audio, so not every AIFF-family file is plain PCM. The format can also hold named chunks for author, copyright and annotations. Common media-type labels are audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff. It is used for audio production on macOS and professional sound editing.

You meet AIFF files in recording sessions, sample libraries and projects exported from Mac audio software. They are lossless but large, so an MP3 is the lighter copy for sharing, uploading or playing on a device that doesn't read AIFF.

### Programs that open AIFF files

**Linux, Mac and Windows**

- Audacity: imports most AIFF files, including all PCM variants, without its optional FFmpeg library.
- VLC media player plays AIFF.
- FFmpeg: lists AIFF encoding and decoding support.

**Mac and Windows**

- Adobe Audition: handles uncompressed AIFF as well as most common compressed variants.

**Mac**

- Logic Pro and Apple Music open AIFF.

### AIFF and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .aiff or .aif with audio/aiff; .mp3 with audio/mpeg.
- **Compression**: AIFF is usually uncompressed PCM and lossless. MP3 is lossy: its encoder models human hearing and drops sound that most listeners would not miss.
- **Size**: uncompressed PCM needs more storage than a compressed copy of the same recording. A 128 kbps MP3 needs roughly an eleventh of the space the matching CD audio does, so 192 kbps lands near one seventh for a CD-rate source.
- **Metadata**: an AIFF stores author, copyright and annotations in named chunks, while an MP3 puts song titles and other tags into ID3 structures kept apart from the audio.
- **Editing**: each time you edit an MP3 and export it again, you add another lossy encoding stage. The AIFF has no such stage.
- **Support**: every major browser plays MP3. MP3 became ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993, and the license program for its patents closed on 23 April 2017.

This page asks LAME for 192 kbps, which a source at 32 kHz or more gets, and keeps only the audio. You can't pick a bitrate here, so if a delivery spec asks for a different one, use a desktop tool from the next section. The AIFF you chose is never changed, and you download a new file named after it with the .mp3 ending. Files chosen together are encoded in sequence, and each produces its own MP3.

### Other ways to convert AIFF to MP3

Each of these re-encodes the audio as a new MP3, as this page does.

- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** begin with File > Import > Audio and pick the AIFF, then File > Export Audio, select MP3 in the format list, set the channels and sample rate, choose the entire project or the current selection, and press Export. The MP3 encoding settings sit on a separate MP3 Export Options page.
- **SoX (command line):** run `sox session.aiff -C 192 session.mp3`. A positive integer after -C is taken as the bitrate in kbps. SoX can only write MP3 if it was built with the LAME library.
- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i session.aiff -c:a libmp3lame session.mp3`. FFmpeg's format list includes AIFF, and its MP3 encoder comes from the external LAME library. FFmpeg falls back on a default bitrate of its own when none is given, so add `-b:a 192k` for the bitrate this page uses.

### Problems with AIFF files

- **An editor rejects the file**: it may be AIFF-C, which extends the family to compressed audio. The family name alone doesn't promise support, because a decoder for the actual compression is needed.
- **The file is huge**: that is normal for uncompressed PCM, which takes plenty of room on a drive or a phone. Make an MP3 for sharing and keep the AIFF as the master.
- **Credits look different in another program**: the author field can show in Audition under Dublin Core: Creator instead of a field called Author.
- **Renaming did nothing**: changing .aif to .mp3 leaves the PCM data inside, because only the label changes. Converting is the only way to make a real MP3.

faqs.question: How do I convert an AMR file to MP3?

faqs.question: Does the converter upload my voice memo?
faqs.answer: No. FFmpeg runs inside your browser, so the memo stays on your device and nothing is sent to a server.

faqs.question: Why is the MP3 so much bigger than the AMR?
faqs.answer: AMR is built to be tiny, and an MP3 spends many more bits on the same speech. A narrowband AMR (8 kHz) comes out near 64 kbit/s, because MP3 at that sample rate cannot go higher. The extra size adds no detail the phone never recorded.

faqs.question: Will the MP3 sound better than the AMR?
faqs.answer: No. AMR was designed for speech over phone networks and samples at 8 kHz. The MP3 is easier to play, but it can't bring back sound that the recording left out.

faqs.question: How do I open an AMR file on my computer?
faqs.answer: VLC media player and QuickTime Player can open AMR, and so can Audacity when it has an AMR-capable FFmpeg library. Converting to MP3 here gives you a file that plays on nearly every device.

faqs.question: Why won't Audacity open my AMR file?
faqs.answer: Audacity needs an FFmpeg library that can decode AMR, and the recommended FFmpeg installer leaves out narrowband AMR. Convert the file here and open the MP3 instead.

faqs.question: What is the difference between AMR and AMR-WB?
faqs.answer: AMR-WB is a separate codec that samples at 16 kHz, while narrowband AMR samples at 8 kHz. The two files carry different signatures, which is why a rename cannot convert one into the other.

faqs.question: Can I convert a batch of AMR voice messages?
faqs.answer: Yes, add all the messages at once. They are processed one by one, and every message comes back as a separate MP3 file.

faqs.question: Can I just rename my .amr file to .mp3?
faqs.answer: No. Renaming changes only the label. The file still holds AMR speech, not MP3 data.

faqs.question: Does the converter reduce background noise?
faqs.answer: No. It decodes the speech as recorded and writes it to MP3, with no noise reduction or level change. Use an audio editor such as Audacity first if you want the recording cleaned up.

guide.title: Understanding AMR for MP3 output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AMR file?

The name AMR is short for Adaptive Multi-Rate. ETSI standardized it for GSM speech, and 3GPP then adopted it for third-generation cellular systems. That history explains what an .amr file usually is: a voice recording or voice message from a phone, saved at a very small size. It is built for voice, not music, which is why it turns up in voice recordings on phones, voice messages and mobile telephony.

Narrowband AMR uses eight speech modes that span 4.75 to 12.2 kbps. It samples at 8 kHz and encodes speech in 20-millisecond frames. AMR-WB is a separate codec with a 16 kHz sampling rate, so the two should not be treated as one format.

RFC 4867, published in April 2007, defines storage files as well as RTP transport. The registered media type for narrowband AMR is audio/AMR. Because AMR was built for speech, a recording that sounds like a phone call is working as designed.

### Programs that open AMR files

**Linux, Mac and Windows**

- VLC opens AMR recordings.
- FFmpeg: a command-line decoder for AMR.
- Audacity: needs a compatible FFmpeg library with AMR decoding enabled, and the recommended installer omits narrowband AMR.

**Mac**

- QuickTime Player opens AMR recordings.

### AMR and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .amr with audio/AMR; .mp3 with audio/mpeg.
- **Purpose**: AMR is a lossy speech codec. MP3 is a general audio format used for music libraries, podcasts and portable players, standardized as ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993, and every major browser plays it.
- **Compression**: both are lossy. AMR compresses speech only, while an MP3 may be encoded at a constant or at a variable bitrate.
- **Bitrate**: narrowband AMR tops out at 12.2 kbps. MP3 runs from 32 to 320 kbps. This page asks LAME for 192 kbit/s, which sources below 32 kHz cannot reach, so an 8 kHz AMR gives about 64 kbit/s.
- **Size**: at 12.2 kbps AMR uses about 1.5 KB of data per second of speech, and at 64 kbit/s the MP3 uses 8 KB, roughly five times as much.
- **Origin**: Fraunhofer IIS began the work on MP3 in the late 1980s alongside other MPEG audio group members, and the format drops sound that, by a hearing model, a listener would not notice.
- **Metadata**: an MP3 keeps its song titles and further tags in ID3 structures apart from the audio.
- **Support**: the patent license program for MP3 closed on 23 April 2017.

The MP3 comes from decoding the AMR and encoding it again with LAME, so it is a second lossy generation of the speech. Only the audio is kept, and the page applies no noise reduction, level change or trimming. The sample rate is not changed. Recordings chosen together are converted in turn, and each gets its own MP3 named after its AMR. The MP3 therefore sounds like the AMR, only in a format that more apps will open. Your original AMR stays as it was, and the MP3 arrives as a new download.

### Other ways to convert AMR to MP3

- **FFmpeg (Windows, Mac, Linux):** type this in a terminal, in the folder that holds the recording: `ffmpeg -i memo.amr -c:a libmp3lame memo.mp3`. FFmpeg's format list includes 3GPP AMR, and its audio codec list says MP3 encoding goes through the external LAME library, which is switched on with --enable-libmp3lame when FFmpeg is built. In it, -i is the input file and -c:a selects the audio encoder. If you set no bitrate, FFmpeg uses a default of its own, so the result is not the file this page makes.

### Problems with AMR files

- **The MP3 still sounds like a phone call**: the recording only holds the narrow speech range that AMR stores, and a higher bitrate can't restore frequencies the recorder never kept. Frequencies that an AMR-WB source would carry are missing from narrowband AMR, because the two codecs use different sampling rates.
- **Audacity refuses the file**: Audacity may reject narrowband AMR even after an FFmpeg library is installed, because the recommended FFmpeg installer excludes that codec.
- **AMR and AMR-WB share an extension**: AMR and AMR-WB storage signatures differ. Changing the extension doesn't change the speech codec.
- **The file opens nowhere**: a player needs a decoder for the codec. Try VLC to see whether it plays.

faqs.question: How do I convert ARW to JPG?
faqs.answer: Choose the ARW above and wait while ImageMagick reads it in your browser. The first file takes a little longer because the image engine loads first. Then save the JPG that appears.

faqs.question: Can I convert many ARW photos together?
faqs.answer: Yes. Drop in a batch of ARW photos and the page converts them in turn, saving a separate JPG for each.

faqs.question: Can I convert ARW to JPG without losing quality?
faqs.answer: Not entirely. A JPG is lossy, so it keeps less than the sensor data in the ARW, and the page passes no quality setting. Keep the ARW if you may want to edit the photo again.

faqs.question: Can I adjust exposure or white balance here?
faqs.answer: No. The page offers no editing controls. For adjustments, develop the ARW in darktable or Imaging Edge Desktop and export a JPG from there.

faqs.question: Do I need Sony software to open an ARW?
faqs.answer: No. This page reads the file in your browser. Sony's Imaging Edge Desktop is useful if you want to view and develop your raw photos yourself.

faqs.question: What happens if the page can't read my ARW?
faqs.answer: The page reports that the picture in the file couldn't be read. Copy the file from the card again and retry, or open it in Imaging Edge Desktop to see whether it is intact.

faqs.question: Is there a size limit for ARW files?
faqs.answer: There is no limit on file size. Only the picture's pixel count matters: above about 537 megapixels the page declines and reports it as too large.

faqs.question: Is the JPG the full size of the photo?
faqs.answer: The page sets no resize option, so the picture is not scaled down. Open the JPG in an editor to check its pixel dimensions.

faqs.question: What file name does the JPG get?
faqs.answer: The download reuses your ARW's name and ends in .jpg, so DSC00001.ARW downloads as DSC00001.jpg. The ARW itself is not changed.

faqs.question: Is my ARW photo uploaded?
faqs.answer: No upload takes place. The decoding runs through ImageMagick compiled to WebAssembly in this tab, so your raw photo never reaches a server. Only the new JPG is written, and the ARW stays untouched.

guide.title: About ARW files
guide.markdown:
### What is an ARW file?

An ARW file is a raw photograph from a Sony camera. Where a JPG is a finished picture, an ARW keeps information straight from the sensor, and software has to develop it into an image you can look at. That is why photographers shoot raw: settings such as white balance and exposure can still be adjusted after the shot, without baking them in.

Sony cameras let you record raw in different ways. The company documents uncompressed, losslessly compressed and compressed options. Lossless compression makes the file smaller and discards no image information, while an uncompressed file is the largest. File size also varies with the camera's sensor, so a high-resolution body produces much bigger ARW files than a small one. You meet ARW files on the memory card of an Alpha camera, and in the folders of anyone who edits their photos. Because the file is meant for processing rather than for sending, it is rarely what you attach to an email or upload to a website, and that is the usual reason people look for a converter.

### Programs that read ARW photos

**Windows and Mac**

- Imaging Edge Desktop: Sony's own program for viewing and developing its raw photos.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- ImageMagick: reads this camera raw format.

**Linux**

- XnView MP: a viewer whose supported-format list includes ARW; private and educational use costs nothing.

### ARW and JPG compared

- **Purpose**: ARW is raw material for editing. JPG is a finished picture for sharing and display.
- **Compression**: an ARW can be uncompressed or losslessly compressed. A JPG is lossy: it splits the picture into 8x8 blocks and throws away the detail the eye notices least.
- **Color depth**: JPG stores 8 bits per color channel. A raw file holds the sensor's own readings, which are the source for the picture you develop.
- **Adjustments**: raw settings can be changed after capture. In a JPG they are already applied.
- **Extensions**: .arw is Sony's raw extension; .jpg and .jpeg are the same format.
- **Reach**: any browser, phone or printer reads a JPG. An ARW needs software that supports the camera.
- **Size**: JPEG typically shrinks a picture by a factor of 10 to 20 against its uncompressed form, which is why the JPG is the copy you send.

On this page, ImageMagick reads the ARW and writes a JPG. There is no slider for quality, exposure or white balance. The JPG is a standard copy, and the ARW stays your master. If you plan to crop, recolor or print the photo, do that work from the raw file in a raw developer, and use this page when you just need a copy that you can send, post or open on any device.

### Other ways to convert ARW to JPG

- **XnConvert:** drag the ARW into the Input tab; on the Output tab choose the destination folder, JPEG as the target format and its quality settings, then click Convert. XnView's format list names Sony RAW with the extension arw.
- **darktable:** in the export module set target storage to file on disk, choose the file format, leave the quality field at its default of 95 or change it, then press Start export.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick input.arw output.jpg`. The output extension decides the format in ImageMagick, and its format list shows ARW as read-only and JPEG as read and write.

### Problems with ARW files

- **A raw converter skips it**: darktable's camera support leaves out Sony ARW 4.0 and 5.0 downsized lossless files in M and S sizes and ARW 6.0 lossy files. Check which recording mode the camera used, or open the file in Sony's Imaging Edge Desktop.
- **The files fill the card**: raw files take a lot of space, and Sony lists one size for uncompressed recording and another for compressed.
- **A lossless ARW is smaller than expected**: lossless compression keeps all the image information, so a smaller file alone doesn't mean damage. Compare it with an uncompressed file from the same camera.
- **It is not ready to send**: raw development is what an ARW is for; a finished picture for sharing is a different job. Convert a copy to JPG and keep the ARW as your master.
- **The page reports an unreadable picture**: re-copy it from the card, ideally using a card reader, then retry.
- **A very large picture stops the conversion**: a picture over about 537 megapixels stops the conversion with a too-large message.

infoArticle.title: About audio and video transcription
infoArticle.markdown:
Audio to Text transcribes speech from audio or video files. Uploaded files are processed in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser for transcription. YouTube, TikTok, SoundCloud, and other webpage links are not supported right now. The speech model downloads on first use and runs locally.

This tool is best for interviews, meetings, lectures, and voice notes. Larger files take longer to process and may use more memory.

**Why use this tool**

- Handles uploads or direct links to audio and video files.
- Creates a plain text transcript you can edit or share.
- Works with common audio and video formats.

faqs.question: Do my files get uploaded?
faqs.answer: Uploads are processed locally in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser. The model files are downloaded when needed.

faqs.question: Which file types are supported?
faqs.answer: Common audio and video formats like MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, FLAC, OGG, OPUS, MP4, MOV, MKV, WEBM, AVI, and M4V.

faqs.question: Can I use YouTube or SoundCloud links?
faqs.answer: Not right now. YouTube, SoundCloud, TikTok, and other webpage links are not supported. Upload the audio or video file, or paste a direct link to one.

faqs.question: Why is the first run slower?
faqs.answer: The speech model downloads the first time you run the tool. After that it is cached for faster use.

faqs.question: What does the output look like?
faqs.answer: You get a plain text transcript (.txt) that you can download or copy.

faqs.question: Why do the colors look banded or grainy?

faqs.question: Is there a limit on the AVI's length or size?

faqs.question: Is my AVI uploaded?

guide.title: About AVI files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVI file?

AVI is short for Audio Video Interleave. Microsoft released it alongside Windows 3.1, with a first specification in 1992. It is a container built on RIFF: a header records things like the frame size and frame rate, and another chunk holds the media, with video and audio interleaved. FOURCC identifiers say which codec each stream uses.

Because AVI can wrap uncompressed, lossless or lossy video, the extension tells you nothing about quality or size. Files normally end in .avi, and video/x-msvideo is a commonly used media type. You find AVI in older Windows video, camera and capture output, and archives of video work. It also turns up in older desktop video workflows, where a file called .avi can hold almost any codec.

### Programs that open AVI files

**Windows / Mac / Linux**

- mpv: plays AVI on the desktop and lets you switch audio and subtitle tracks.
- ffplay: bundled with FFmpeg; whether a file plays depends on decoders for the video inside.

**Windows and Mac**

- VLC media player: plays AVI.
- Adobe Premiere: imports AVI when the necessary decoder is available.

**Windows**

- Windows Media Player: plays AVI.

**Mac**

- QuickTime Player: plays AVI.

**Mobile**

- On Android and iOS, VLC plays AVI, though decoding hinges on the codec inside the file.

### AVI and GIF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .avi, usually video/x-msvideo; .gif and image/gif.
- **What they are**: AVI is a video container. GIF is an image format that can hold many frames and times them in hundredths of a second.
- **Compression**: AVI can carry many codecs. GIF uses lossless LZW coding on every frame.
- **Timing**: a GIF holds many images and sets the delay between them in hundredths of a second. This page builds its GIF at 15 frames a second.
- **Colors**: no GIF frame can use more than 256 colors from its palette. GIMP likewise reduces a GIF export to 256 colors at most, which can change gradients.
- **History**: CompuServe released GIF in 1987, and GIF89a followed in July 1990 with transparency, timing for each frame, comments and application blocks. Unisys started charging LZW license fees in 1994. The US patent lapsed in 2003, while the matching patents in Europe and Japan lasted until 2004.
- **Transparency**: one palette color of a GIF can be marked fully transparent, and there is nothing in between. Soft transparent edges can't keep partial opacity in a GIF.
- **Sound**: AVI can carry audio. GIF cannot.
- **Support**: every major browser displays GIF, in a web page or a message.

For this pair, the page reads the AVI with FFmpeg in your browser. It makes a palette from the video and then writes the GIF with it. The frame rate is 15 per second, the longer side is at most 480 pixels, and the loop repeats forever. The audio is not carried across, and nothing is trimmed. A 1920 by 1080 AVI comes out 480 by 270, since the longer side is capped at 480 pixels and the proportions stay the same.

### Other ways to convert AVI to GIF

- **Ezgif Video to GIF (website):** choose the AVI, or enter a direct video URL, and upload it. Enter the start and end times in seconds, then pick a size and a frame rate. The size menu has presets such as Original (up to 800px), 600xAUTO and 480xAUTO, and higher frame rates look smoother but make a larger file. With no start and end it makes a GIF from the first five seconds. The site allows files up to 200 MB, and the maximum length is 60 seconds at 5 frames a second and 30 seconds at 10. Your video is uploaded, and the site deletes uploaded files an hour later.

### Problems with AVI files

- **The file plays without picture or sound**: an editor can recognize AVI but still lack the decoder for what is inside. The container does not say which codec the stream uses; the FOURCC identifiers do.
- **A large capture won't open**: AVI's original size limits are tighter than the later OpenDML extension allows, so big captures need software that supports it.
- **The picture is stretched**: aspect ratio and scan type information are handled differently by different AVI programs. Check the video in more than one player.

faqs.question: How do I convert AVIF to GIF?

faqs.question: Will an animated AVIF become an animated GIF?
faqs.answer: No. An animated AVIF contributes only its first frame, which leaves the GIF as one still picture. Keep the AVIF, or use a program that handles image sequences, when the motion matters.

faqs.question: Why do the colors look banded or flat in the GIF?

faqs.question: What happens to transparency in the AVIF?

faqs.question: Is my AVIF's HDR or 10-bit color kept?
faqs.answer: No. Only 8 bits per channel get through, so a 10-bit or 12-bit AVIF loses its extra depth, and GIF then holds each frame to 256 colors.

faqs.question: Why am I told my browser can't open the AVIF?

faqs.question: Are the AVIF's EXIF, color profile and XMP copied?
faqs.answer: No. Raw pixels are all that pass through, so that information is dropped. The GIF holds only the picture.

faqs.question: Can I rename .avif to .gif instead?

faqs.question: Can I convert many AVIF files at once?

guide.title: About AVIF and GIF
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVIF file?

The Alliance for Open Media created AVIF, the AV1 Image File Format. The Alliance was founded in 2015 to build royalty-free media formats and published the AV1 video codec in 2018. Version 1.0.0 of the AVIF specification is dated 19 February 2019. A file stores AV1-coded images inside the HEIF container, and it can be lossy or lossless, transparent, a still or an image sequence, with up to 12 bits per channel for HDR and wide color gamut. Exif, XMP and an ICC color profile fit inside, and image/avif is the registered media type.

Websites use AVIF for web images with small files and for HDR and wide-gamut pictures. You meet it when a site serves a photo in it and your software, or an upload form, won't take the file. That is the usual reason to convert. A Baseline-profile image item is at most 8,192 by 4,352 pixels, and a larger picture is stored as a grid of such images.

### Programs that open AVIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP gained AVIF import and export in version 2.10.22, which came out in October 2020.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads AVIF, so check your install's format list.
- **Windows:** Microsoft's AV1 Video Extension and its HEIF Image Extension must both be installed before .avif files display.
- **Web:** Edge 121, Safari 16.1, Firefox 93 and Chrome 85 all display AVIF, though without progressive rendering.
- **Mobile:** Android has decoded AVIF since version 12; Safari on iOS 16 brought in still AVIF images, and that first support leaves out animation.

### AVIF and GIF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .avif is image/avif and .gif is image/gif.
- **Compression**: AVIF uses AV1 and can be lossy or lossless. GIF compresses losslessly with LZW coding, and each image uses a palette of at most 256 colors.
- **Color**: AVIF supports up to 12 bits per channel, HDR and a wide color gamut. A GIF image is limited to its palette of 256 colors.
- **Metadata**: GIF89a offers comments and application data, a different set from the fields an AVIF carries.
- **Transparency**: AVIF supports it. In a GIF one palette entry can be designated fully transparent, and there are no partial transparency levels.
- **Animation**: a GIF can hold many images, with the delay between them set in hundredths of a second. GIF came from CompuServe in 1987; its GIF89a revision, dated July 1990, brought in the extensions for transparency and frame timing.
- **Support**: GIF displays in every major browser. GIF patents on LZW ran out in 2003 in the US and in 2004 in Europe and Japan.

Your browser decodes the AVIF here, and ImageMagick then writes the GIF. An animated AVIF gives its first frame only. Everything goes through 8-bit RGBA, which drops EXIF, ICC and XMP data, and you get one still picture for software that wants a GIF. Keep the AVIF if you need the sequence, the extra bit depth or the metadata again.

### Other ways to convert AVIF to GIF

- **GIMP on Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP 2.10.22 or later can open the AVIF; then choose File > Export As. Type .gif as the Name field's extension, or choose GIF under Select File Type, and export. GIMP only supports exporting a GIF with a maximum of 256 colors.
- **ImageMagick (command line):** run `magick input.avif output.gif`. ImageMagick's format list shows AVIF and GIF as formats it reads and writes.
- **Pillow (Python):** Pillow reads and writes AVIF, 8-bit only. Call `Image.open` on the file, then `save` with a name that ends in .gif; Pillow infers the format from that ending when you name none.

Each of these writes one still picture unless you set up an animation yourself. Check the result at its normal display size, because palette reduction shows most on photos and gradients.

### Problems with AVIF files

- **The AVIF won't open**: older browsers may fail to display it. Update the browser, or ask the site for a JPEG, PNG or WebP copy.
- **An older GIMP can't import it**: releases before 2.10.22 lack the AVIF importer.
- **A 10-bit file fails on a phone**: baseline 8-bit AVIF decodes on Android 12 and newer, but support for 10-bit is optional.
- **Windows shows no preview**: the .avif viewer needs the AV1 Video Extension and the HEIF Image Extension.
- **It decodes slowly**: decoding an AVIF is slow, and encoding one may take several seconds.

faqs.question: What happens to transparency in an AVIF?

guide.title: About AVIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVIF file?

An AVIF file is a still picture, or a short run of pictures, encoded with AV1 and wrapped in a HEIF container. The Alliance for Open Media wrote it. That group formed in 2015 to build media formats free of royalties, and AV1 itself came out in 2018. Release 1.0.0 of the AVIF specification carries the date 19 February 2019, and the media type is image/avif.

Inside one file you can have lossy or lossless coding, an alpha channel, an image sequence, and color depth as high as 12 bits for each channel, which covers HDR and wide gamut. Exif, XMP and an ICC profile can ride along. AVIF is royalty-free. In the Baseline profile a single image item can be no wider than 8,192 pixels or taller than 4,352, with 8,912,896 pixels as the total, and larger pictures are stored as a grid of such images. The price is processing time: AVIF decodes slowly, and encoding a single image may take several seconds. Most people meet it on the web, in browsers that support it.

### Programs that open AVIF files

**Windows**

- Microsoft's AV1 Video Extension and HEIF Image Extension: needed before .avif files display.

**Web**

- Chrome 85, Firefox 93, Safari 16.1 and Edge 121 were the first releases to show AVIF. Those browsers are what lets this page work at all.

**Mobile**

- Android: AVIF decoding starts at version 12.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- GIMP: has imported and exported AVIF since version 2.10.22 (October 2020).
- ImageMagick: its formats table lists AVIF as readable and writable.

### AVIF and JPEG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .avif goes with image/avif. The .jpg and .jpeg endings both go with image/jpeg and mean the same format.
- **Compression**: AVIF applies AV1 coding in lossy or lossless form. JPEG splits the picture into 8x8 blocks, runs each through a cosine transform, and packs the result with Huffman codes; the usual baseline mode is lossy.
- **Transparency**: AVIF has an alpha channel, and JPEG does not.
- **Color depth**: AVIF goes to 12 bits a channel; JPEG stops at 8.
- **Animation**: AVIF can store a sequence, while a JPEG is exactly one picture.
- **Metadata**: AVIF can hold Exif, XMP and an ICC profile, and the JPEG written here holds none.
- **Compatibility**: every major browser displays JPEG. AVIF depends on an up-to-date browser or on software from the list above.

Converting swaps AVIF's compact files and extra precision for that wider acceptance. The page decodes the AVIF in your browser, flattens it into 8-bit RGBA pixels, and writes the JPEG with quality set to 0.85.

### Other ways to convert AVIF to JPEG

- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux):** load the AVIF in GIMP 2.10.22 or later, then File > Export As (Shift+Ctrl+E) saves a JPEG copy. A dialog with a quality setting follows, and its default is 85.
- **ImageMagick (command line):** run `magick input.avif output.jpeg`. The command takes an input file and an output file, and the output's extension picks the format.
- **avifdec (command line):** run `avifdec input.avif output.jpeg`. The quality defaults to 90 for JPEG output, and only the first frame of a sequence is decoded unless you name another with --index.

### Problems with AVIF files

- **An editor refuses the AVIF**: that program lacks an AVIF decoder or has an outdated one. Convert the file here, or update the software. GIMP releases before 2.10.22 lack the AVIF importer.
- **Windows shows no preview**: AVIF needs the two Microsoft extensions listed above before it displays.
- **An older browser draws nothing**: AVIF is a recent format, so offer visitors a JPEG, PNG or WebP fallback.
- **The JPEG has a solid background where the AVIF was clear**: JPEG can't store transparency. The [AVIF to PNG converter](/avif-to-png/) keeps it.
- **You expected motion but got one frame**: an animated AVIF yields its first frame only. Hold on to the AVIF if you need the animation.
- **Colors differ from the original**: HDR range and bit depth beyond 8 don't carry over to the JPEG, and the color profile isn't copied. Keep the AVIF for showing on capable screens.
- **A phone can't open the file**: Android decodes AVIF from version 12, so older systems need an app or browser with its own decoder.

faqs.answer: Pick the AVIF above and the JPG downloads after it is decoded. A batch of AVIF files yields one JPG for each.

faqs.question: Can you convert AVIF to JPG without losing detail?
faqs.answer: Some detail can go. The AVIF is decoded to pixels and saved again as a lossy JPG at quality 0.85.

faqs.question: What happens to an AVIF's HDR and wide color?
faqs.answer: A JPG stores 8 bits per channel, so the extra bits an HDR AVIF can carry, up to 12, don't come along. The JPG is made from decoded pixels only, so the AVIF's ICC profile, EXIF and XMP are dropped too.

faqs.question: What happens to an animated AVIF?
faqs.answer: You get a JPG of its first frame. The other frames are left out.

faqs.question: Why does the page say it can't open my file?
faqs.answer: Your browser decodes the AVIF itself. So an older browser without AVIF support can't read it, and the page then says "This browser can't open … files". Switch to a current browser such as Chrome or Firefox.

faqs.question: Why won't AVIF files open on my Windows PC?
faqs.answer: To show AVIF, Windows needs two Microsoft Store add-ons, the HEIF Image Extension and the AV1 Video Extension. Without them, open the file in a browser or convert it here.

faqs.question: Does a batch of AVIF files come out as one download?
faqs.answer: No. Each AVIF becomes its own JPG download, and the page makes no ZIP.

faqs.question: Can I convert AVIF to JPG on my phone?
faqs.answer: Yes, in a mobile browser that shows AVIF, such as Chrome on Android or Safari on iPhone. Each JPG downloads like any other file.

faqs.question: Is AVIF the same as HEIC?
faqs.answer: No, though both use the HEIF container. AVIF compresses its pictures with AV1 and HEIC with HEVC, so each needs its own decoder.

faqs.question: Why do websites use AVIF?
faqs.answer: It makes small files for web images and suits HDR and wide-gamut pictures, and it is royalty-free.

guide.title: About AVIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVIF file?

Each AVIF file is an AV1 Image File Format picture: compressed with the AV1 video codec and stored inside a HEIF container, the container family iPhone photos use. It comes from the Alliance for Open Media, a body formed in 2015 to build royalty-free media formats; it released AV1 in 2018. AVIF specification version 1.0.0 bears the date 19 February 2019.

AVIF can be lossy or lossless, keep transparency, hold image sequences and store up to twelve bits per channel, which suits HDR and wide-gamut color. The cost is speed: AVIF images are slow to decode, encoding one can take several seconds, and they don't draw progressively while loading.

Its uses are web pictures that need small files and HDR or wide-gamut images, and nobody owes royalties for it.

### Programs that open AVIF files

- **Windows:** before .avif files open, Windows needs two Microsoft add-ons: HEIF Image Extension alongside AV1 Video Extension.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP handles AVIF import and export from version 2.10.22, released in October 2020. ImageMagick reads AVIF files from the command line.
- **Web and mobile:** Google Chrome from version 85 and Safari from 16.1 display AVIF. Chrome's support is for the browser only; it doesn't mean every viewer on your system opens AVIF. This page relies on the browser's support, since your browser does the decoding.
- **Web:** Firefox from version 93 and Edge from 121 display AVIF.
- **Mobile:** Android decodes AVIF from version 12.

### AVIF and JPG compared

- **File endings**: .avif is image/avif, while .jpg and .jpeg are image/jpeg.
- **Compression**: AVIF stores AV1-coded images, lossy or lossless. JPEG cuts the picture into 8x8 blocks, and its baseline mode is always lossy.
- **Color depth**: AVIF goes up to 12 bits per channel, with HDR and wide gamut. JPEG stores 8 bits per channel.
- **Transparency**: AVIF has an alpha channel. JPG has none.
- **Sequences**: AVIF can hold an animation. A JPG holds one frame.
- **Image size**: AVIF's Baseline profile caps one image item at 8,192 x 4,352 pixels; a bigger picture is split into a grid of items.
- **Loading**: a progressive JPEG shows a coarse version first and sharpens. AVIF appears only once decoded.
- **Layers**: a JPEG cannot store layers, and the JPG made here is one flat picture.
- **Licensing**: AVIF is royalty-free, and JPEG's US patents expired in 2006.
- **Metadata**: Exif, XMP and an ICC profile can sit in an AVIF, but none of them go into the JPG made here.

JPEG's namesake is the Joint Photographic Experts Group, whose committee started work in 1986; its core standard reached ISO/IEC 10918-1 in 1994. Cameras and scanners widely write it. The JPG gives up AVIF's extra color precision and its transparency, and every major browser displays it. This page decodes the AVIF with your browser and writes the JPG at quality 0.85. Your AVIF stays untouched; the JPG is a new copy you download.

### Other ways to convert AVIF to JPG

- **GIMP (Windows, Mac and Linux):** version 2.10.22 or later opens the AVIF; export it as a JPEG with File > Export As.
- **ImageMagick (terminal):** run `magick input.avif output.jpg`.
- **avifdec from libavif (command line):** run `avifdec input.avif output.jpg`. The `-q` option sets the JPEG quality, 90 by default. With an image sequence, avifdec stops at the first frame unless `--index` asks for a different frame or for every frame.

### Problems with AVIF files

- **"This browser can't open … files"**: your browser has no AVIF decoder. Update it, or switch to Chrome 85+, Firefox 93+, Safari 16.1+ or Edge 121+.
- **Windows can't show it**: add both Microsoft extensions, or open the file in a browser.
- **A big image takes a while**: AVIF images are slow to decode, so give a large file a moment.
- **GIMP won't open it**: versions older than 2.10.22 have no AVIF importer.
- **See-through areas are lost**: JPG has no alpha channel. The [AVIF to PNG converter](/avif-to-png/) keeps transparency.
- **An animation gives one picture**: a JPG holds a single frame, so only the first is kept.
- **Changed the ending by hand**: an AVIF renamed to .jpg still holds AV1 data inside. Convert the file instead.
- **An upload form doesn't accept AVIF**: convert the file here and upload the JPG.

faqs.question: How do I convert AVIF to PNG?
faqs.answer: Add an .avif file through the converter on this page. Your browser decodes it, the page saves the pixels as a PNG, and the PNG is yours to download. Nothing goes to a server.

faqs.question: How do I change an AVIF to PNG on Windows or a Mac?
faqs.answer: Open this page in the browser on that computer, choose the file and download the PNG. A GIMP version that imports AVIF can also export a PNG.

faqs.question: Does the PNG keep the transparent background?
faqs.answer: Yes. Transparency is kept for PNG output, so the see-through areas of the AVIF stay see-through.

faqs.question: Why is my PNG a different size from the AVIF?
faqs.answer: PNG compression is always lossless, so it keeps every pixel the browser decoded, while an AVIF may be lossy and uses AV1 coding. The two sizes can differ widely. For a lossy file instead, convert to JPG or WebP.

faqs.question: Is converting AVIF to PNG lossless?
faqs.answer: Mostly. Writing the PNG loses nothing, since it keeps the 8-bit pixels your browser decoded. Any loss from the AVIF's own compression stays, and depth beyond 8 bits per channel is dropped.

faqs.question: Will an HDR AVIF look the same as a PNG?
faqs.answer: Not always. Each channel is reduced to 8 bits and no color profile is copied, so keep the AVIF if you want to view it in HDR.

faqs.question: What happens to an animated AVIF?
faqs.answer: An animated AVIF becomes a single PNG showing its first frame.

faqs.question: Should I convert AVIF to PNG or JPG?
faqs.answer: PNG keeps transparency and every decoded pixel; JPG is lossy and has no transparency. Pick by what the picture needs.

faqs.question: What does "This browser can't open AVIF files" mean?
faqs.answer: Your browser has no AVIF decoder. The message recommends updating to a recent Safari, Chrome, Edge or Firefox.

faqs.question: Can I convert more than one AVIF file at a time?
faqs.answer: Yes. Add several AVIF files and each gets converted in sequence into a separate PNG. No ZIP is created.

guide.title: About AVIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVIF file?

AVIF, the AV1 Image File Format, comes from the Alliance for Open Media. In 2018 the alliance, founded in 2015 to create royalty-free media formats, released the AV1 video codec. The AVIF specification's 1.0.0 version carries the date 19 February 2019. An AVIF file stores AV1-coded images inside the HEIF container.

AVIF handles lossy or lossless compression, transparency and image sequences, and allows 12 bits per channel for HDR and a wide color gamut. Exif data, XMP and an ICC color profile are other things a file can contain. The format is royalty-free, yet decoding is slow and encoding a picture can take several seconds. In the Baseline profile one image item may be 8,192 pixels wide, 4,352 high and 8,912,896 pixels in total, and a bigger picture is built as a grid of such images.

The registered media type is image/avif. Browsers that display AVIF include Chrome 85 and later, Firefox 93 and later, Safari 16.1 and later and Edge 121 and later, and AVIF does not render progressively.

### Programs that open AVIF files

**Linux, Mac and Windows**

- GIMP: import and export were added in version 2.10.22.
- ImageMagick: reads AVIF; inspect the installed format support.

**Windows**

- Windows viewers: to show .avif files you need Microsoft's HEIF Image Extension plus its AV1 Video Extension.

**Web**

- Firefox: browser support, not a guarantee that every operating-system viewer opens AVIF.

**Web and Mobile**

- Chrome: Android decodes AVIF from version 12.

**Mobile**

- Safari: added still AVIF images on iOS 16.

### AVIF and PNG compared

- **Compression**: AVIF can be lossy or lossless. PNG is lossless every time, using DEFLATE, which is a mix of LZ77 and Huffman coding.
- **Bit depth**: AVIF allows up to 12 bits per channel. PNG allows 1 to 16 bits per sample. The PNG written here has 8 bits per channel.
- **Transparency**: both support it.
- **Animation**: AVIF supports image sequences. Animated PNG is covered by the current specification, and a program unable to animate shows the default still image.
- **Metadata**: AVIF may hold Exif, XMP and an ICC profile. PNG's third edition allows Exif in an eXIf chunk. This page copies none of them.
- **Patents**: AVIF is royalty-free, and PNG carries no known royalty-bearing patents.
- **Origins**: PNG came about as a patent-free replacement for GIF. It was also the first format the W3C published as a Recommendation, in October 1996, and both RFC 2083 and ISO/IEC 15948:2004 describe it.
- **Structure**: a fixed signature opens every PNG, and then come chunks such as IHDR (the header), IDAT (pixel data) and IEND (the final one).
- **Display**: every major browser displays PNG. AVIF displays in the browsers named above, loads only once it is fully decoded instead of sharpening as it arrives, and is slow to decode.
- **Where you meet PNG**: Mac screenshots arrive as PNG files, and the format is a common pick for transparent logos and sharp web graphics.
- **Media types**: image/avif and image/png.

What this page does: your browser's own image decoder reads the AVIF, and the page writes the pixels into a PNG, which has no quality setting. Everything goes through 8-bit RGBA, so a 10-bit or 12-bit source loses its extra depth. For an animated AVIF, only the first frame is used. There is no size limit of its own.

### Other ways to convert AVIF to PNG

- **GIMP (Windows, Mac and Linux):** open the AVIF in a GIMP version able to import it, then File > Export As (Shift+Ctrl+E) lets you export it as a PNG.
- **avifdec (command line):** run `avifdec input.avif output.png` with the libavif tools. The `-d` option sets 8 or 16 bits per channel. Only the first frame of an image sequence is decoded unless `--index` names another frame, or all of them.

### Problems with AVIF files

- **A picture won't display**: older browsers may fail to display AVIF. Supply a JPEG, PNG or WebP fallback.
- **GIMP can't open the file**: older GIMP releases lack the AVIF importer introduced in version 2.10.22.
- **A phone can't decode it**: Android 12 and later handsets and tablets support baseline 8-bit AVIF decoding, and 10-bit decoding is optional.
- **A PNG is the wrong choice**: for a smaller photo, use the [AVIF to JPG converter](/avif-to-jpg/) or the [AVIF to WebP converter](/avif-to-webp/).
- **"Image decode failed."**: the browser couldn't decode the file. Save a fresh copy from its source.

guide.title: About BMP and JPG
guide.markdown:
### What is a BMP file?

Windows Bitmap (BMP) is a raster image format introduced with Microsoft Windows. Microsoft owns the BMP family, which first served Windows and OS/2. Pixel data is normally stored uncompressed, so programs can read and write a BMP with little effort, at the cost of large files. Lossless compression is available as an option, in the form of run-length encoding. Version 5 arrived with Windows 98 in 1998 and gained room for an ICC profile plus an alpha channel.

BMP turns up as Windows screen captures and system graphics, and as simple Windows graphics and uncompressed image interchange. The registered media type is image/bmp.

### Programs that open BMP files

- **Windows:** Paint and Photos open BMP.
- **Mac:** Preview opens BMP.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP opens BMP. ImageMagick reads BMP images. XnView MP names BMP among its formats, though company use of XnView MP needs a license.
- **Web:** Firefox displays BMP pictures, and Mozilla's compatibility table lists Chrome as supporting them.

### BMP and JPG compared

- **Extensions**: BMP is .bmp (image/bmp); JPG is .jpg or .jpeg (image/jpeg).
- **Compression**: BMP is usually uncompressed. JPG is lossy. In baseline JPEG, each 8x8 block of pixels is transformed with a discrete cosine transform, after which Huffman coding packs the result. ITU-T T.81 dates from 1992 and ISO/IEC 10918-1 from 1994.
- **File size**: an uncompressed BMP can be bulky.
- **Bit depth**: a BMP may use anywhere from 1 to 32 bits per pixel; the JPG made here is written from 8-bit RGBA pixels.
- **Transparency**: BMP version 5 can have an alpha channel. JPG has none.
- **Metadata**: BMP version 5 can carry an ICC profile. The page's JPG carries none.
- **Progressive mode**: a progressive JPEG paints a blurry whole first and sharpens it as the rest loads; depth is 8 bits per channel either way.
- **Reach**: every major browser displays JPEG, and digital cameras and scanners commonly output it.
- **Editable content**: neither file keeps editable vector shapes or live text: a BMP stores plain pixels and a JPG cannot store layers, so neither reopens as an editable project.

The page decodes the BMP with your browser's own image decoder and writes the pixels as a JPG at quality 0.85 through the browser's canvas. No metadata is copied, and the original BMP is not changed: you download a new JPG.

Quality is usually set on a 0 to 100 scale, and the same number can mean different quality in different programs. This page has no slider, so every JPG from it uses the same setting.

### Other ways to convert BMP to JPG

- **IrfanView:** choose File > Open for the BMP, then File > Save as, pick JPG as the output format and set the new file name. IrfanView's format list marks both BMP and JPG as readable and savable.
- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux):** after opening the BMP, go to File > Export As, call the file capture.jpg and press Export. The JPEG dialog has a Quality setting from 0 to 100, and GIMP's page says JPEG supports neither transparency nor multiple layers.
- **ImageMagick (command line):** run `magick capture.bmp -quality 85 capture.jpg`. ImageMagick's format list shows BMP and JPEG as readable and writable.

### Problems with BMP files

- **The file is enormous**: a BMP commonly stores uncompressed pixels, so it can be bulky. For sharing, PNG or JPEG is easier to pass around.
- **Old software wants a different bitmap header**: software that expects an older header might want BMP3 or BMP2 output, not the default BMP version. That concerns writing a BMP, not producing a JPG.
- **The transparent area is gone**: JPG has no transparency. A BMP with an alpha channel is a version 5 bitmap, and that channel has nowhere to go in a JPG. For transparency, the [BMP to PNG converter](/bmp-to-png/) is the place to go.
- **The page can't open the bitmap**: the browser's decoder rejected the file. Open it in an image editor and save it again.
- **Quality numbers don't match between programs**: 85 in GIMP or ImageMagick may not produce the same JPG as this page's 0.85. Pick one tool for the whole batch.
- **You need to edit shapes or text later**: a BMP holds pixels only, so keep the original project file.

guide.title: About BMP files
guide.markdown:
### What is a BMP file?

The BMP format, a bitmap image family from Microsoft, was used first on Windows and OS/2. Its name is short for bitmap, and the file stores a grid of pixels. The format commonly keeps those pixels uncompressed, though lossless compression is available. Windows 98 brought version 5 in 1998, which can store an ICC profile as well as an alpha channel.

You come across BMP in Windows screen captures and system graphics, and in files saved by old programs that never moved on to a compressed format. Its media type is image/bmp. The format is simple to read and write but produces large files, and it was designed around the Windows display rather than the web. It can store 1 to 32 bits per pixel, with optional run-length compression. Different BMP versions use different headers, so a program written for an old one can trip over a newer file. A BMP does not keep vector shapes or live text, only the pixels. Run-length compression, where offered, is lossless too, so a compressed BMP and an uncompressed one can hold identical pictures.

### Programs that open BMP files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- XnView MP: BMP is among the formats it lists; companies need a license.
- ImageMagick: reads BMP.
- GIMP: opens BMP.

**Windows**

- Paint and Photos on Windows open BMP.

**Mac**

- Preview: opens BMP.

**Web**

- Firefox displays BMP in the browser. Mozilla's browser compatibility table lists Chrome as supporting BMP images as well.

### BMP and PNG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: BMP files end in .bmp and PNG files in .png, with the types image/bmp and image/png.
- **Pixel storage**: both formats keep a grid of pixels rather than shapes or text.
- **Compression**: a BMP is usually stored uncompressed. PNG compression is always lossless and uses DEFLATE, a mix of LZ77 and Huffman coding.
- **Color depth**: PNG holds 1 to 16 bits per sample, indexed, grayscale or truecolor. This converter passes the picture through 8 bits per channel.
- **Transparency**: PNG offers an optional alpha channel. Only BMP version 5 can match it, since older BMP files lack one.
- **Structure**: structurally a PNG is a signature plus a run of chunks, where IHDR comes first, IDAT holds the picture and IEND is last.
- **Origin**: PNG was made as a patent-free successor to GIF. It became a W3C Recommendation in October 1996 and is also ISO/IEC 15948.
- **Support**: PNG displays in every major browser and has no known royalty-bearing patents. macOS also saves screenshots as PNG by default.
- **Animation and HDR**: the current PNG specification covers animated PNG (APNG, media type image/apng); software without animation falls back on the default still image. Its third edition supports HDR through the cICP chunk.
- **Newer features**: PNG's third edition became a W3C Recommendation on 24 June 2025 and lets Exif metadata sit in an eXIf chunk.

What changes in this conversion is the packing. The page reads the BMP with your browser's image decoder and writes the same pixels into a PNG. Metadata such as an ICC profile stays behind. Nothing here trades detail for size, as a JPEG conversion would. Several BMP files convert one after another, each to its own PNG, so a folder of old screen captures can be handled in one visit.

### Other ways to convert BMP to PNG

- **ImageMagick (command line):** run `magick diagram.bmp diagram.png`. ImageMagick reads and writes both BMP and PNG, and it writes BMP version 4 by default, with BMP3 and BMP2 selecting older headers.

### Problems with BMP files

- **The file is large**: a BMP usually stores every pixel uncompressed, so an uncompressed BMP can be bulky. PNG or JPEG can suit sharing better.
- **A program rejects the BMP**: software built for an older bitmap header may want BMP3 or BMP2 instead of the default BMP version. PNG sidesteps the issue.
- **The BMP has an ICC profile**: version 5 can record one, and this converter does not copy it into the PNG. The pixels are written as your browser decodes them.
- **A transparent area shows as a solid color**: alpha belongs to BMP version 5, and older BMP files have none, so there is nothing for the PNG to keep.
- **The picture is pixelated after you enlarge it**: BMP stores pixels, not shapes. Enlarging it, or converting it, cannot add detail that was never there.
