guide.title: About WMA and MP3 files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WMA file?

WMA stands for Windows Media Audio, a family of audio codecs developed by Microsoft. The sound sits inside Microsoft's ASF container, and the .wma ending marks an ASF file that holds audio only. The family has four variants: standard WMA, WMA Professional, WMA Lossless and WMA Voice. WMA 9 supports variable bitrate encoding. The media type usually given is audio/x-ms-wma.

WMA serves delivery workflows and is sometimes used to store audio between editing steps. You find WMA files in Windows media libraries and on older portable music players. The extension does not tell you which of the four variants a file uses, which is why an app can open one WMA and refuse another.

### Programs that open WMA files

**Linux, Mac and Windows**

- VLC media player: its feature list names ASF/WMA input and several Windows Media Audio decoders.
- Audacity: imports unprotected WMA once its optional FFmpeg library is installed.
- FFmpeg: decodes WMA 1 and 2 plus the Pro, Voice and Lossless variants, per its support list.

**Windows**

- Windows Media Player: the format's own player, named in the format reference.

### WMA and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .wma with audio/x-ms-wma, against .mp3 with audio/mpeg.
- **Container**: WMA is held in an ASF container, while an MP3 is audio frames with ID3 tags attached.
- **Compression**: the standard WMA codec is lossy, and WMA Lossless is not. MP3 is always lossy.
- **Ownership**: WMA is a proprietary Microsoft format. MP3 is an ISO/IEC standard (11172-3) from MPEG, developed at Fraunhofer.
- **Bitrate**: WMA 9 supports variable bitrate. MP3 can be constant or variable and runs from 32 to 320 kbps.
- **Metadata**: the title and artist of a WMA sit in its ASF container. The MP3 written here carries them as ID3 tags when FFmpeg finds them.
- **Reach**: MP3 plays in every major browser and on nearly every device.
- **Typical use**: WMA belongs to Windows media libraries and older portable players; MP3 serves music libraries, podcasts and portable players.

MP3 is lossy, and its encoder uses a model of what people can hear to decide which sounds to leave out. This page decodes the WMA with FFmpeg and asks LAME for 192 kbps, which only sources sampled at 32 kHz or higher can reach. A run on a sample WMA decoded the WMA and wrote a new MP3 stream. The sound is first decoded and then encoded again, so the MP3 is a new file and not a repackaged WMA. A lossless WMA therefore ends up lossy, so keep a WMA Lossless original and make the MP3 as a listening copy.

The download is named after the WMA, with .mp3 in place of .wma. A folder's worth of WMA files can go in together; they are processed one by one, which means an album gives one download per track. No size limit or timeout is set.

### Other ways to convert WMA to MP3

- **FFmpeg (Windows, Mac, Linux):** type `ffmpeg -i input.wma -c:a libmp3lame output.mp3` in a terminal.
- **Audacity with FFmpeg (Windows, Mac, Linux):** get Audacity's optional FFmpeg library first, open the WMA, choose File > Export Audio and select MP3 in the Format menu. Protected WMA files do not import.

Audacity's MP3 export lets you set the bit rate mode, and in FFmpeg you can pass -b:a with a rate of your choice. This page offers neither.

### Problems with WMA files

- **Audacity cannot import it**: the optional FFmpeg library may be missing, or the file is copy-protected. Install the library or use an unprotected copy.
- **A player opens one WMA but not another**: an app may decode one WMA codec and not another, and the ending hides which variant a file is.
- **A lower bitrate than 192 kbps**: sources at 16 to 24 kHz are held to 160 kbps by LAME, and sources at 8 to 12 kHz to 64 kbps.
- **The file is cut short**: a damaged or truncated WMA usually still converts, to a shorter MP3.
- **Titles or artists are missing**: FFmpeg copies the WMA's global tags, such as title and artist, when it has them. Fill in the rest with a tag editor.
- **Audition will not import it**: Adobe Audition enables WMA import on Windows only, once DLMS Format Support is switched on.

faqs.question: How do I convert WMV to MP4?
faqs.answer: Choose the WMV file, wait while FFmpeg re-encodes it in your browser and save the MP4. Nothing is uploaded, so the time depends on your device.

faqs.question: What video and audio does the MP4 contain?

faqs.question: Will the quality drop?
faqs.answer: It can. The WMV is decoded and encoded again with a lossy codec, so detail can be lost that a plain copy would have kept. Convert the original WMV once and don't re-convert the MP4.

faqs.question: Does my 4K or 60 fps WMV keep its size and frame rate?
faqs.answer: Not if it exceeds the limits. The longer side shrinks to 1920 px at most and motion is capped at 30 frames a second, with extra frames dropped and the length unchanged. A smaller video isn't enlarged, and both sides are rounded down to even numbers.

faqs.question: My WMV was interlaced. Is that fixed?
faqs.answer: The converter applies the yadif deinterlacing filter to frames marked as interlaced, which removes the comb pattern on moving edges. Frames that aren't marked pass through it unchanged.

faqs.question: Will the MP4 start playing before it has finished downloading?
faqs.answer: It can, if it is served over the web. The converter moves the MP4's index to the front of the file, so a player has what it needs at the start.

faqs.question: Why did the conversion fail?
faqs.answer: The message begins "FFmpeg failed with exit code" and ends in the exit number. A stream that FFmpeg only partly decodes is one cause, since its own list describes one Windows Media Video decoder as not completely working; an unusual file can fail even when Windows plays it.

faqs.question: Can I convert several WMV files at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. Add them together and the page converts each in order, giving you a separate MP4 every time. Nothing is zipped, and no size limit is set.

faqs.question: Does it run on a phone or a Mac?
faqs.answer: It runs inside the browser, so the work happens on your own device wherever the page opens. Mac users who prefer an app can use HandBrake, which lists WMV among its source types.

faqs.question: Is the MP4 smaller than the WMV?
faqs.answer: The page makes no promise. A run of its own settings on a small test clip gave a file a little smaller than the WMV, but the result depends on the video.

guide.title: About WMV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WMV file?

Windows Media Video is Microsoft's video codec family, and a .wmv file wraps Windows Media content in the ASF container, short for Advanced Systems Format. ASF was built to keep audio and video synchronized and to stream from a disk or over HTTP. Inside you may find Windows Media Video 7, 8 or 9 compression. The Library of Congress lists video/x-ms-wmv as a commonly used media type, not an IANA registration.

The format is proprietary and counts as a legacy one, and its compression is lossy. The container holds audio and video streams side by side.

Streaming through Windows Media, screen recordings and older Windows video are where WMV appears, and its listed players are Windows Media Player and VLC media player.

### Programs that open WMV files

**Linux, Windows and macOS**

- The VLC media player lists ASF/WMV input and decodes Windows Media Video 1, 2 and 9.
- Bundled with FFmpeg, FFplay plays WMV through its decoders.

**Windows**

- Windows Media Player is listed among the players.

**Mobile**

- On Android, VLC carries over the desktop player's decoding features.
- Local files on iPhone and iPad play in VLC for iOS, which uses a player of its own instead of the system one.

### WMV and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .wmv with video/x-ms-wmv; .mp4 with video/mp4.
- **What they are**: WMV puts Microsoft's own codecs in an ASF container. MP4 is MPEG-4 Part 14, ISO/IEC 14496-14, first published in 2003, and it grew from the ISO Base Media File Format.
- **Structure**: QuickTime calls them atoms, the nested boxes an MP4 consists of.
- **Support**: every major browser plays MP4, and VLC, QuickTime Player and Windows Media Player open it. WMV needs decoders for Windows Media.
- **Typical use**: MP4 serves online video, phone and camera recordings, and shared video files. WMV mostly holds older Windows video.
- **Streams**: MP4 carries subtitles and chapters, and it holds codecs such as H.264, H.265 and AV1 for the picture.
- **Extensions**: video MP4 files use .mp4 or .m4v, while audio-only MPEG-4 files often use .m4a.

This converter decodes the WMV and encodes new H.264 video and AAC audio. It limits the longer side to 1920 px and the rate to 30 fps, deinterlaces frames marked as interlaced, and writes the MP4 with its index at the front.

### Other ways to convert WMV to MP4

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i legacy.wmv -c:a aac -c:v libx264 shared.mp4`. It leaves out the size and quality settings this page uses, so supply your own when a destination demands them. To put the index first as this page does, add `-movflags +faststart`, which makes a second pass that moves the moov atom to the start of the file.
- **HandBrake:** choose Open Source on the toolbar and pick the WMV, which the source-formats page lists. Choose a preset, such as the default Fast 1080p30, which writes MP4 with H.264 and AAC stereo and which the quick-start page calls fast and compatible with most devices. Set Save As and the To folder, then select Start.

### Problems with WMV files

- **The file opens but shows no picture**: a player may parse the ASF wrapper yet lack the matching video decoder, since reading the container and decoding its video are different jobs.
- **A player has no decoder**: knowing the container does not mean a decoder exists for the video or audio inside it, so try VLC.
- **Quality isn't set by the extension**: a .wmv can hold a high-quality recording or a very compressed one, so judge by the picture.
- **The MP4 can look softer than the WMV**: the new encode is lossy. Resolution and frame rate limits also apply.
- **Converting twice makes it worse**: each lossy pass can remove detail, so go back to the WMV and convert from there.
- **Fast motion looks less fluid**: footage above 30 fps has frames dropped here, though the clip keeps its length and is not slowed down.
- **An MP4 that won't play**: a write cut short can leave an incomplete MP4 that won't play, so copy it again when it came from a download.
- **Big files take long**: the work runs on your device with a single-threaded encoder. Trim the video first if it is only partly needed.

faqs.question: What does a malformed XML error with a line and column mean?

faqs.question: What happens to comments and the DOCTYPE?
faqs.answer: They stay in the listing in gray, and nested elements are indented two columns for each level.

guide.title: About XML files
guide.markdown:
### What is an XML file?

XML stands for Extensible Markup Language. The W3C developed it from a subset of SGML, and the fifth edition of XML 1.0 became a W3C Recommendation in November 2008. A document has a single root element with properly nested content, made of elements, attributes, character data and entities. A conforming processor must accept UTF-8 and UTF-16.

XML describes structure, not appearance. The tags are yours to define, so an invoice, a sitemap, a feed and a configuration file are all XML but mean different things. RFC 7303 defines the application/xml media type and treats text/xml as its alias. You meet XML in data exchange between systems, in configuration files and in feeds and sitemaps. Plain XML says nothing about fonts, page size or colors, so there is no single correct way to print it, and that is why a converter has to choose one.

### Programs that open XML files

**Windows / Mac / Linux**

- Visual Studio Code: opens XML source in its XML language mode.
- xmllint: reads XML and reports parsing errors; it comes with libxml2.

### XML and PDF compared

- **What they are**: XML is text that structures data, and PDF fixes content onto pages. PDF pages can hold text next to vector graphics and raster images, and a PDF can add links, bookmarks and forms.
- **Extensions and media types**: .xml with application/xml; .pdf with application/pdf.
- **Origin**: Adobe's Camelot project started in 1991 and was PDF by 1992. It was meant to capture a document from any application and display or print it identically anywhere. ISO 32000-1 adopted PDF 1.7 in 2008.
- **Fonts**: fonts must be embedded in a PDF for it to look identical on every system.
- **Validation**: well-formed syntax does not show that the data satisfies a DTD or an application schema.

The XML to PDF page does not render the file. It prints a listing: one line for each node, with every element followed by its attributes in source order and indented two columns for each level, down to 20 levels. Text sits beside its element when that is all the element holds. CDATA keeps its lines. Comments, processing instructions and the DOCTYPE are gray.

The encoding is taken from the byte order mark, a UTF-16 `<?`, or the XML declaration, in that order, and otherwise the file is read as UTF-8 and then Windows-1252. Elements nested deeper than 20 levels share the indent of the 20th. Text lines inside an element are trimmed, and a long line wraps with its continuation indented. The listing is for reading and review, for example to send someone a file they would rather not open in an editor. It is not a byte-exact copy, so keep the XML as your source.

The pages are A4 portrait with 3/4 inch margins, in 10 point type on 12 point lines, with no header, footer or page numbers. A file whose text is entirely Windows-1252 is set in Courier, and any other character sets the whole file in DejaVu Sans.

### Other ways to convert XML to PDF

- **Apache FOP (command line):** pass the XML and a stylesheet to FOP and name the PDF with -pdf, as in `fop -xml report.xml -xsl layout.xsl -pdf report.pdf`. The stylesheet has to turn your XML into valid XSL-FO, because plain XML does not define a page layout.

### Problems with XML files

- **Tags don't match**: an unclosed element, overlapping elements or a second root element stops a strict parser. Fix the line and column the error names.
- **A schema is not checked**: a file that passes here is well formed, which says nothing about whether its contents are right for the program that will use them.
- **An undeclared entity**: a strict parser can reject a reference to an undeclared entity as a well-formedness error, while this page shows any entity beyond the five built-in ones as written.
- **A repeated attribute**: XML forbids repeating an attribute on one element, but the parser used here accepts it and the listing keeps only the first value.
- **The file has no content**: a file holding only whitespace and control characters is refused by this page as empty, and a file with no element at all is refused as malformed.
- **The encoding is wrong**: bytes that disagree with the declared character encoding make the file unreadable. Save a UTF-8 copy and fix the declaration.

faqs.answer: The XML Paper Specification, a Microsoft document format standardized as ECMA-388. An XPS file is a ZIP package of XML pages with fixed layout, often produced when Windows prints to a file.

infoArticle.title: About YouTube transcription
infoArticle.markdown:
YouTube to Transcript transcribes speech from audio or video files. Uploaded files are processed in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser for transcription. YouTube, TikTok, SoundCloud, and other webpage links are not supported right now. The speech model downloads on first use and runs locally.

This tool is best for interviews, meetings, lectures, and voice notes. Larger files take longer to process and may use more memory.

**Why use this tool**

- Handles uploads or direct links to audio and video files.
- Creates a plain text transcript you can edit or share.
- Works with common audio and video formats.

faqs.question: Do my files get uploaded?
faqs.answer: Uploads are processed locally in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser. The model files are downloaded when needed.

faqs.question: Which file types are supported?
faqs.answer: Common audio and video formats like MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, FLAC, OGG, OPUS, MP4, MOV, MKV, WEBM, AVI, and M4V.

faqs.question: Can I use YouTube or SoundCloud links?
faqs.answer: Not right now. YouTube, SoundCloud, TikTok, and other webpage links are not supported. Upload the audio or video file, or paste a direct link to one.

faqs.question: Why is the first run slower?
faqs.answer: The speech model downloads the first time you run the tool. After that it is cached for faster use.

faqs.question: What does the output look like?
faqs.answer: You get a plain text transcript (.txt) that you can download or copy.
